setup: This is about the line y = mx + b, or whether a relation is a function at all.

steps.say: In y = mx + b the m is the slope, so it can be read straight off the coefficient of x.
The b is the y-intercept: the value of y when x is 0, which is the point where the line crosses the y-axis.
A non-vertical straight line hits any vertical line at exactly one point, so it passes the vertical line test and defines a function.

Here x is pinned to a single value, which makes the relation a vertical line. A vertical line meets most vertical lines at a whole point rather than one, so it fails the vertical line test and is not a function.
